Sets or removes taints on one indexed Node — key=value:Effect or key:Effect to set, --remove to drop one. The effect is NoSchedule, PreferNoSchedule or NoExecute.

One index only, as for kx drain: a NoExecute taint evicts every Pod that does not tolerate it, so tainting a range of Nodes in one command drains each of them. Setting one asks first, unless you pass --yes.

kubectl's own taint flags pass through, --overwrite and --dry-run among them. --all and --selector are refused, since beside a Node's name kubectl taint applies them to every Node they select.

A flag kx doesn't know is refused; put it after `--` to pass it through to kubectl.

## Usage

```text
kx taint [OPTIONS] <index> [taint...] [kubectl flags]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `<index>` | Row number from the current listing, or @name for a mark; kx state or kx mark shows them |
| `[taint]...` | A taint to set, key=value:Effect or key:Effect; repeatable |

## Options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run[=string]` | client or server to preview the change without making it, as kubectl takes it; kx's line says nothing was changed |
| `-o, --output string` | Output format, as kubectl takes it; kubectl's output is printed, and kx's own lines go to stderr |
| `--remove strings` | Taint to remove, as key or key:Effect (repeatable) |
| `-y, --yes` | Skip the confirmation prompt a NoExecute taint asks |

## Passthrough options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--allow-missing-template-keys` | If true, ignore any errors in templates when a field or map key is missing in the template. Only applies to golang and jsonpath output formats. |
| `--field-manager string` | Name of the manager used to track field ownership. |
| `--overwrite` | If true, allow taints to be overwritten, otherwise reject taint updates that overwrite existing taints. |
| `--show-managed-fields` | If true, keep the managedFields when printing objects in JSON or YAML format. |
| `--template string` | Template string or path to template file to use when -o=go-template, -o=go-template-file. The template format is golang templates [http://golang.org/pkg/text/template/#pkg-overview]. |
| `--validate[=string]` | Must be one of: strict (or true), warn, ignore (or false). "true" or "strict" will use a schema to validate the input and fail the request if invalid. It will perform server side validation if ServerSideFieldValidation is enabled on the api-server, but will fall back to less reliable client-side validation if not. "warn" will warn about unknown or duplicate fields without blocking the request if server-side field validation is enabled on the API server, and behave as "ignore" otherwise. "false" or "ignore" will not perform any schema validation, silently dropping any unknown or duplicate fields. |
| `…` | kubectl's global flags too: `--context`, `--kubeconfig`, `--as` and the rest; `kubectl options` lists them |

## Global options

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--no-color` | Disable styled output |
| `-h, --help` | Show this message and exit |

## Examples

```bash
kx taint 1 dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule
kx taint 1 --remove dedicated
kx taint 1 maintenance:NoExecute -y
kx taint 1 dedicated=infra:NoSchedule --overwrite
kx taint 1 maintenance:NoExecute --dry-run=server
```
